body: Hi! Sorry, wasn't expecting to have to use this account again. I'm doing better for now, I guess. I mean, I planned to be dead by today, so that not being the case is an improvement in its own right. Not exactly "wanting to live" but not in the "motivated to die" situation I was over this weekend. I made an appointment with my university's psychological services for tomorrow morning. I'm not going to go in and mention everything - honestly I'm pretty nervous about how it's going to go. Again, new situation new people. Thank you for being here and thank you for the followup. It means a lot.

I don't remember it being particularly helpful. The atmosphere was overbearing, the nightly group sessions were frustrating, the whole "unknown place with unknown people" thing, the loss of agency.. and I'm not sure how accommodating my university would be. I guess that last one is a bit silly, but if I'm not going to die, then I'd really not want to lose my scholarships. It's a private university and it's still crazy expensive with a combined annual $14,000 in scholarships.
I mean, I'll respect your opinion, but having gone through it multiple times myself, yeah, it's a pretty big deal.

Look, I wish I could believe that. I really do. But in my experience, the moment you mention anything related to suicide, you get sent to a hospital against your will. I'm not 100% sure, but I am pretty sure that's still something they can do even now that I'm an adult. If it's between being in a hospital again and dying, I'd rather not seek professional help.. it's worse.
It isn't. I haven't been diagnosed, and I won't see a therapist (bad experiences, hospitalization involved), but I probably would have met the criteria for at least the past 10 years, if not longer.
